title: Whole-body 3D kinematics of freely behaving Drosophila
source_locator: Results 2.5; Fig. 5c-d; Methods 'Fly husbandry and behavioral experiments'; Supplementary Video 5 legend
quote: Illuminating the arena with a red LED reliably elicited sustained running bouts, which we tracked with a modified headless skeleton
mapping_basis: Paper names the neuron DNg100, a MANC type name; the split line VT058557-GAL4.AD; R85F12-GAL4.DBD is listed in driver_lines.csv as the BDN2/DNg100 split.
stimulation: red LED flashlight illuminating the arena (intensity and duration not stated); flies fed all-trans retinal 1 day before; white strobe imaging light also noted as able to activate CsChrimson
sensory_condition: decapitated, free on the floor of a glass/3D-printed corridor chamber, white strobe illumination
coordination_notes: 3D joint kinematics of induced running fall within the wild-type running principal-component space; less femur and tibia flexion than wild-type running (Fig. 5c-d)
n_flies_note: number of flies not stated; n=50 speed-matched running cycles analysed per condition (Fig. 5d)
notes: Demonstration experiment in a methods paper. Fig. 5c shows repeated L1 tarsus-tip step trajectories after 'red light ON', and joint kinematics for foreleg, midleg and hindleg. The Supplementary Video 5 legend says 'The fly speeds up when the red light turns on', so the fly may already have been moving before the light came on. That, the unstated n_flies and the lack of a no-retinal control are why labeler_confidence is medium. Running in all six legs is coded yes for all pairs (PROTOCOL 3, walking). Surface coded 'other' (free on the chamber floor, not a ball or slippery surface).
